Subject: Quick ask: temporary tether for our POC GPUs

Lukas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the inference numbers looked promising. We're trying to firm up internal procurement for the POC and have one operational ask: can Redwood provide a short tether (soft hold) for 8x H100-equivalent slots during our two-week sprint window in mid-August?

We expect an initial burst of ~1.2M tokens/day for validation runs, then taper to a steady-state of ~300k tokens/day. Critical constraints:
- Prefer H100 or equivalent for mixed-precision training inference
- Max contiguous window: Aug 14 - Aug 28 (can shift ±2 days)
- Budget range: open to a short-term reserved rate or committed burst credits

I've attached a quick usage sketch (capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx) and asked Cal to run a finance sensitivity. If Redwood can provision a soft hold and confirm fallback options (e.g., A100 80GB with quantization profile), we can sign the MOA and move to the POC kickoff.

Best,
Ellen

Moped Systems

Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: temporary tether for our POC GPUs

Team — I ran an initial slot-level scan for Aug 10-30 across our US pools. Summary (high level):
- H100 pool: 12 slots free in primary pool (SFO/ORD) but 5 are already promised to soft-holds for other trials. Net available: 7
- A100 80GB: plenty of capacity (18 free) but expected tail-latency is ~12–18% higher for the specific model they demoed unless we apply 4-bit quantization and KV cache tweaks
- Mixed-sku fallback plan looks feasible: 4x H100 + 4x A100 with automatic routing based on latency-load would cover their profile if we accept a documented 5–10% variance in p95 latency

Operational constraints / asks to confirm:
- If they require strict H100 parity across all runs we need a written commitment (either short reserved or refundable credit) to prevent preemption; otherwise we can offer the mixed-sku fallback and a 24hr SLA to escalate to H100 when available.
- We should lock a soft hold in the capacity ledger (internal ticket) and surface it to Dedicated scheduling to prevent accidental reallocation.

I've attached a CSV with the raw node mapping and baseline p95 samples (poe_latency_profile.csv). I recommend a soft hold for 8 slots with an explicit fallback to A100 for non-critical batches. Lukas — if you want, I can generate the formal inventory ticket and estimate a short-term reserved cost.

— Ben
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Attachment: poe_latency_profile.csv (CSV stub)

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@mopedsys.com>
To: lukas.meyer@redwood.com
Cc: caleb@capexconsult.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: temporary tether for our POC GPUs

Thanks, Ben — that mapping is helpful. Answering Lukas' questions:
1) H100-equivalent is preferred but not strictly required for all runs. The first 48 hours of validation need the lowest p95; after that we can tolerate the mixed-sku approach if we document it in the runbook.
2) Concurrency: peak concurrency will be 64 simultaneous streams during synthetic validation, but average concurrent inference will be ~12 during the steady-state period. We’ll provide exact session profiles on Friday.
3) Compliance: all runs can occur in our shared cloud region (US) — no special VPC or on-prem needed.

We can commit to an initial refundable credit (details in the attached MOA) to secure the soft hold — Caleb is copying the finance ask. If Redwood can provide an ops-ready fallback and a formal soft-hold ticket by next Tue (30 Jul), we can sign the MOA and finalize kickoff dates.

Best,
Ellen

Attachment: moped_poc_mopedsys_signed_MOA.pdf (pdf stub)
